digest.top_line: BEACON-HCC: 96.6% concordance with expert allocation vs 72.4% for BCLC 2025, elevating SBRT and TARE to preferred options in early and locally advanced HCC.
digest.tldr: One hepatobiliary item: a 20-expert North American Delphi framework that promotes SBRT and TARE out of BCLC's systemic-first lanes. Class 1C names TARE or SBRT over TACE when selective delivery is feasible (each ORR >50%), and Class 3B leans on NRG/RTOG1112 for macrovascular invasion. Concordance is agreement with expert opinion, not outcomes.

sites.intro: A consensus allocation framework, not a trial: it moves SBRT and TARE earlier in HCC, on expert agreement rather than outcome data.

verdict.rationale: Expert-consensus framework that re-allocates BCLC advanced-stage disease to local therapy, contesting BCLC 2025 rather than confirming it. Pilot validates against expert opinion, not outcomes.
verdict.audience: HCC, all stages, including Vp1-4 macrovascular invasion and distant metastases

studies.significance: Classes 1D and 3B sit at BCLC advanced (C), systemic-only territory; BEACON names SBRT and TARE as options there, leaning on NRG/RTOG1112 (Vp3/4 in 63%, OS trend p=0.06 vs sorafenib) and DOSISPHERE. The counterweight is Class 4A, where EBRT is explicitly not indicated outside palliation.
studies.monday_clinic: In Vp1-2 invasion with a deep durable response to local or systemic therapy, this frames transplant as reachable after 12 months of stability within Milan criteria, a route BCLC advanced staging closes; it does not extend to Vp3/4 or regional nodal disease, which XXL and VITALITY excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Modified **Delphi** consensus, **20** North American experts across hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology and radiation oncology, with iterative discussion and repeat voting. Piloted on **29** real-world cases against external expert recommendations.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Covers the full HCC spectrum, **Class 1A** (unifocal ≤3 cm) through **Class 4B** (distant metastases), with Vp1-4 vascular invasion split across Classes 1D, 3B and 4A. Symptom-directed care is the default for **ECOG PS ≥2** or **Child-Pugh ≥B9** ineligible for transplant.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **EBRT and SBRT are named allocation options, not salvage**, across Classes 1A to 3B. SBRT is credited with high local control in Class 1A/1B, and **TARE or SBRT are preferred over TACE** for Class 1C when delivered selectively (**ORR >50%**). Class 4A is the cutoff.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: External expert decisions matched BEACON in **28 of 29** cases (**96.6%**) vs **72.4%** for BCLC 2025.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: BCLC 2025 routes Class 1D and 3B to **advanced (C)**, i.e. systemic therapy; BEACON opens both to TARE, SBRT or resection in selected cases. Class 4A moves the opposite way, to **systemic therapy only**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents North American multidisciplinary HCC practice across Class 1A through 4B, including Vp1-4 macrovascular invasion. Does not represent Child-Pugh C or ECOG PS ≥2 patients, for whom symptom-directed care is the stated default.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The validation cohort was a second North American expert group scoring **29** cases, so concordance partly reflects shared practice culture rather than framework accuracy. The weakest initial-round agreement was **11/16 (68.8%)**, and repeat voting left dissent, with respondents arguing TARE and one arguing SBRT should be **preferred** rather than useful.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SBRT enters the allocation grid from Class 1A through 3B rather than sitting downstream of TACE: for Class 1C, TARE or SBRT are preferred over TACE when deliverable selectively (ORR >50%). Class 4A is the stated limit, EBRT not indicated outside palliation.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Adjuvant therapy after complete response to surgical or locoregional treatment is explicitly not recommended, and ICI plus TACE stays case-by-case rather than routine. Systemic therapy remains the cornerstone for Classes 3B, 4A and 4B, with subgroup data showing equal efficacy in main portal vein invasion.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Resection is preferred without CSPH, transplant with it, and the framework pushes candidacy later: patients converting after locoregional or systemic response should be reconsidered for surgery. Class 3B cites an RCT where resection after neoadjuvant radiation outperformed up-front resection.

papers.title: BEACON-HCC: Best evidence and north american consensus on treatment allocation for hepatocellular carcinoma
authors: on behalf of HCC-Live Steering Committee
papers.abstract: Background : Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. Optimal treatment decisions are challenging, and existing treatment allocation frameworks may not fully reflect the evolving therapeutic landscape or contemporary clinical practices in North America. Methods : Using a modified Delphi process, a multidisciplinary panel of 20 North American experts in hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology, and radiation oncology developed a consensus-based treatment framework for HCC, termed the BEACON-HCC system. The framework was informed by current evidence and expert opinion through iterative discussion and voting. In a pilot study using 29 real-world patient cases, we assessed concordance between external expert recommendations and BEACON-HCC recommendations and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) 2025 treatment recommendations. Results : The BEACON-HCC treatment allocation framework diverges from prior frameworks by incorporating nuanced clinical features such as degree of intrahepatic tumor burden and vascular invasion, and adverse tumor prognostic markers, to align treatment allocation with tumor biology and therapeutic potential. Key innovations include the incorporation of emerging modalities such as external beam radiation therapy (EBRT), transarterial radioembolization (TARE), and systemic-locoregional combination therapies. In the pilot exercise, expert treatment decisions showed 96.6% concordance with BEACON-HCC recommendations and 72.4% concordance with BCLC recommendations. Conclusions : BEACON-HCC is a consensus-based framework for treatment allocation that incorporates the expanding range of therapeutic options available to patients in the North American HCC population. Expert treatment decisions showed a high concordance with the BEACON-HCC system; further validation using empiric clinical data is planned through the HCC-Live Consortium.
